name: Mountain View
label: Mountain View
about_prose: Mountain View is the largest of Bend's 13 neighborhood districts by area. The Mountain View Neighborhood District was established in February 2003 and now covers more than 5,000 tax lots, bounded by Highway 20 to the south, Eagle Road to the east, Butler Market Road to the north, and Shepherd Street to the west. The neighborhood association calls it one of the fastest-growing parts of the city, and the mix on the ground backs that up: single-family blocks, apartment and condo clusters, senior housing, and a regional hospital campus, all cut through by two working irrigation canals.

Those canals, the Pilot Butte Canal and the North Unit Main Canal, are older than the neighborhood around them. The Pilot Butte Canal dates to 1904, when the Pilot Butte Development Company began digging it as Central Oregon's first large-scale irrigation project, opening the high desert around Bend to homesteading. A stretch of it between Cooley Road and Yeoman Road, cut through basalt bedrock with horse-drawn equipment and steam drills and finished on February 10, 1905, was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2016 for the tooling marks still visible in the rock. Central Oregon's irrigation districts are now converting long stretches of open canal to buried pipe to cut water loss, and Bend Park and Recreation has been planning a canal-side trail through the district since at least 2022. Farmland infrastructure from a century ago is slowly turning into a walking route.

Housing here is mostly single-family, built between the 1970s and the early 2000s as Bend's east side filled in, with newer infill adding apartments, condos, townhomes, and retirement and assisted-living housing on top. That build-out means Mountain View does not have the century-old streets or mature tree canopy of Bend's west side. It runs on wide arterials and subdivisions built in the last fifty years, not a historic core built over the last hundred and twenty. For a buyer who wants a historic, walkable core, that is the honest trade-off. For a buyer who wants space, a straightforward floor plan, and easy highway access, it is the point.

St. Charles Bend, a 292-bed regional medical center at 2500 NE Neff Road, is the neighborhood's biggest fixed feature and Bend's largest single employer. The hospital and the streets around it fall inside the city's Medical District Overlay Zone, a special land-use designation built around the campus. For anyone who works at St. Charles or in the clinics that have grown up around it, this is the shortest commute in Bend.

The Forum Shopping Center, along Highway 20 near 27th Street, has anchored the neighborhood's retail for years, with Safeway and Whole Foods among its tenants. Costco was part of that lineup too, but the warehouse club relocated to a new Bend site by early 2025, and its old Costco building at the Forum, more than 150,000 square feet on about 12 acres, has been on the market for lease since. Retail centers change tenants. The location does not: Mountain View residents reach a full grocery and big-box corridor without leaving the east side.

Mountain View Senior High School, at 2755 NE 27th Street, opened in 1979 as Bend's second high school and enrolled about 1,261 students in the 2023-2024 school year as part of the Bend-La Pine district. It offers Advanced Placement classes and Project Lead the Way, and its FFA chapter runs about 165 students under advisor Jeff Papke, most headed for careers that touch agriculture without necessarily owning a farm. For a neighborhood built out by families and hospital workers, having a full comprehensive high school inside its own boundaries matters more than any ranking.

Recreation is the other constant. Pine Nursery Park, 159 acres at 3750 NE Purcell Boulevard, holds 16 pickleball courts, eight of them lit for night play (the Bend Pickleball Club funded more than 60 percent of the original courts and still maintains them), four softball fields, a 14-acre off-leash dog area, a fishing pond stocked by the Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife, and a disc golf course, with a fifth and final phase of lighted courts targeted for fall 2026. Al Moody Park, 16.7 acres at 2225 NE Daggett Lane, keeps about 60 percent of its land in natural vegetation, including a protected rock ridge that still supports native juniper, quail, and rockchucks alongside a treehouse play garden and a winter sledding hill. Pilot Butte State Scenic Viewpoint sits in the western part of the district, a 4,141-foot cinder cone reached by a 0.9-mile trail with a 360-degree view of the Cascades and the city below.

Put together, Mountain View suits people who want to be close to work, whether that is the hospital, the Forum corridor, or a quick run onto Highway 20, and who do not need a historic-district address to feel at home. It is Bend's largest neighborhood district by area and one of its fastest-growing, still filling in around irrigation canals dug for farmland more than a century before the first subdivision went in.

amenities.name: Mountain View Senior High School
amenities.description: A Bend-La Pine Schools grades 9-12 campus at 2755 NE 27th Street with about 1,261 students. Opened in 1979 as Bend's second high school, it offers AP courses, Project Lead The Way, and an agriculture program.

amenities.name: Pine Nursery Park
amenities.description: A 159-acre community park at 3750 NE Purcell Blvd with a 16-court pickleball complex (8 lighted), four softball fields, a 14-acre off-leash dog area, an all-abilities playground, an ODFW-stocked fishing pond, and 4.5-plus miles of paved trails.

amenities.name: Al Moody Park
amenities.description: A 16.7-acre park at 2225 NE Daggett Lane with a treehouse play garden, a fitness trail, a winter sledding area, and a butterfly garden, with about 60% preserved as natural vegetation.

amenities.name: Pilot Butte State Scenic Viewpoint
amenities.description: An Oregon State Parks cinder cone at 1310 NE Hwy 20, its 4,141-foot summit reached by a 0.9-mile nature trail with 360-degree Cascade and city views.

amenities.name: St. Charles Bend
amenities.description: A 292-bed regional medical center at 2500 NE Neff Road in the neighborhood's Medical District Overlay Zone, with emergency, surgery, cardiology, oncology, and orthopedics.

amenities.name: The Forum Shopping Center
amenities.description: A regional center at 2550 NE Hwy 20 with over 400,000 square feet of retail, anchored by Costco, Safeway, Whole Foods, and Barnes and Noble.
amenities.access: Adjacent to the neighborhood along Hwy 20
